findings.file: plugins/audit/tests/_harness.py:688-706 (stage_workers) with tools/sweep-selftests.py default_jobs CI branch
findings.issue: The stage pool was sized for a premise the phase itself contradicts, and it does not consult the sweep pool it now shares cores with. P127.1 sizes for a 'two-core windows-latest runner' (stage_workers docstring; description), but run 38324787932 printed 'sweep: 331 files, 2 workers', which default_jobs() only prints for 4 cpus (cpus-2), and P127.2's own ci.yml comment says the same ('16.7 minutes of suites on two workers'). On a 4-vCPU runner stage_workers(4) == 2, so test_drive_phase's wall time has a floor of (serial stage sum)/2: the task's own numbers are 438-459s serial on macOS, i.e. ~220s on an idle mac pair before any Windows process-start penalty, against the 280s STAGE_TIMEOUT and 300s file cap. Before the phase it had up to 6 children. P127.2 then gives the sweep every core under CI=true (4 workers) and costliest-first submission, so in the shard holding test_drive_phase (shard 2 in the committed table, with test__invariants 118, run_test_gate 60, full_gate 57 started beside it) about 5 processes contend for 4 cores while the heavy staged suite is capped at 2 of them. The same cap now also applies to test_audit_task and test_close_phase (both staged_main users, both in shard 1), which the task did not mention or measure. Worst case the two pools multiply (4 sweep workers x 2 stage workers = 8 runnable on 4 cores); the typical case is the opposite, a heavy suite starved of the cores its siblings have already freed. Nothing handed shows the margin: the only evidence is macOS with 14 cores.
findings.resolution: Read the per-file seconds from CI run 38370435884 (jobs 'selftests (windows-latest, plain 2/3)' and shard 1) before accepting this. If test_drive_phase is above ~150s there, size the pool from the machine the sweep leaves free rather than a fixed half: e.g. have run_one export the sweep's worker count in the child env and let stage_workers use max(2, min(STAGE_WORKERS, cpus - sweep_jobs + 1)), or under CI=true give a staged suite min(STAGE_WORKERS, cpus). Correct the 'two-core runner' wording in the stage_workers docstring, the P127.1 description and sr12's label, and extend sr12 to pin the CI case.

findings.issue: A leg can now be dropped from CI with gate-parity green. Before this diff a leg ran iff its step existed in ci.yml, which sweep_leg_drift compares against verify.sh. Now a step runs only if the matrix contains its leg and its `if:` spells it the same: `leg: [plain, cp1252, spaced]` plus the `include` e2e cells. shard_matrix_drift checks only the `shard: [1, 2, 3]` list. Deleting `cp1252` from the `leg:` list, typing `matrix.leg == 'cp1252 '` or `'cp1251'` in a step, or removing the `include` e2e cells leaves every step present in ci.yml, so the leg comparison passes while that leg (or all launcher steps and the runner's own --selftest) never runs. This is exactly the 'leg silently not run' class the parity gate exists for, and the prove-gates row added (shard: [1,2]) only mutates the shard list.
findings.resolution: Extend shard_matrix_drift (or a sibling) to read every `matrix.leg == '<x>'` in an `if:` and require each <x> to be produced by the matrix (in `leg:` or an `include` entry, and not excluded for every os), and each produced leg to have a step; add a prove-gates TABLE row mutating `leg: [plain, cp1252, spaced]` to drop one, and an ALLOW row for the over-fire.

findings.issue: sr12 pins the stage_workers() table and that the default is within 2..STAGE_WORKERS, but not that run_stages() uses it. Reverting the one-line wiring (`if workers is None: workers = stage_workers()` back to `workers=STAGE_WORKERS`) leaves sr12 and every sr case green, so the behaviour the task names (the pool respects the machine) is pinned only as a pure function. The executor's redFirst is not-attempted, so no run shows otherwise.
findings.resolution: Add a case that runs run_stages over a fixture of labels with a recording stub (or patches stage_workers to return 1) and asserts the concurrency actually used, so the wiring is the thing that fails.

findings.issue: The comments and CONTRIBUTING.md say a stale cost table 'costs balance, never coverage', but sh7 asserts set(sh_costs) <= set(sh_full), so deleting or renaming any swept file turns the sweep's own selftest red (in the e2e cell and in whichever shard holds that file) until someone re-records .github/sweep-costs.json. Either the guard or the sentence is wrong. The table is also one macOS 12-worker run (platform darwin, workers 12); test_commit_task_work is recorded at 57s although P127.1 brought it to ~15s, so the balance is already stale on its first day.
findings.resolution: Pick one: drop the subset requirement from sh7 and keep only 'loads, and times most files', or keep it and say in the comments that a rename must re-record the table. Re-record the table from the CI run after P127.1/P127.2 land.

findings.issue: The header's 'longest selftests: 24m59s' bound reasoning and `timeout-minutes: 60` were sized for one job per OS; every cell now targets 4-7 minutes, so a hung cell holds a runner for an hour and the comment's own rule (a bound under twice the figure is refused, and the figure is re-measured when a job changes) has not been applied to the new shape. Job check names also changed from 'selftests (os)' to 'selftests (os, leg shard)' (17 cells), so any branch-protection required-check entry for the old names (not in the repo, unverifiable here) would never report.
findings.resolution: After run 38370435884, rewrite the 'longest selftests' line to the longest cell and set timeout-minutes to at least twice it; confirm the required-checks list on the remote names the new cells or a single aggregate job.
